# Psalm 113 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Hallelujah! Praise the LORD, all you who serve him! Praise the name of the LORD!

**2** May the LORD's name be praised now and forever!

**3** From sunrise to sunset, the LORD's name deserves to be praised!

**4** The LORD is exalted above every nation; his glory rises higher than the heavens!

**5** Who is like the LORD our God? He sits enthroned in the highest place,

**6** yet he stoops down to look at what's happening in heaven and on earth.

**7** He lifts the poor out of the dirt; he pulls the needy up from the garbage pile

**8** and seats them alongside leaders — right next to the most important people in the nation.

**9** He gives the childless woman a family, turning her into a happy mother. Hallelujah!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **113:5-6**: This is one of the most beautiful descriptions of God in the Bible: he's so high up that he has to look DOWN to see heaven — and yet he bends even further to notice the poorest person on earth. That's who God is.

- **113:7-9**: From the dirt to the throne room. From barrenness to motherhood. God doesn't just help people — he reverses their entire situation. That's the Hallelujah.

— PNEUMA
